messages:
sam_ops: Notifying the channel 55 — sa-east-1 warm pool is failing to reach target after midnight change window. Warm pool at 61%. Node agents returning `kms:Decrypt AccessDenied` and occasional upstream 502s.

nina_infra: timeline of infra changes in region?

sam_ops: two related changes: (1) KMS alias pruning to remove deprecated alias `alias/old-keystore` completed at 00:05, (2) small firewall micro-update to tighten outbound egress rules at 00:12 that added a new deep-inspect rule for telemetry hosts. Failures start ~00:17.

rachel_sre: sample log from a failing node: `2026-04-15T00:18:42Z node-agent error keystore.Decrypt AccessDenied principal=arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/spot-provisioner req=xx-abc`. Also saw `upstream returned 502` from keystore-proxy for same req id.

maria_security: the inspection change included TLS rewrap for certain FQDNs. If the appliance rewraps TLS it may drop the client cert on rewrap. Keystore expects mutual-TLS to assert the principal; without it the proxy rejects with 403/AccessDenied.

sam_ops: that would match the sequence: KMS pruning might have removed a fallback alias, so failed cert auth + missing alias -> mixed 403/502 and some requests just fail earlier.

rachel_sre: important note: CloudTrail shows a ~20s gap in KMS decrypt events for the time window. That makes audit coverage fuzzy for root cause. We need to preserve evidence.

maria_security: agreed. Immediate mitigation: three-pronged: (A) add temporary allowlist in firewall to bypass inspection for `keystore.internal` from warm-pool CIDRs, (B) reintroduce a temporary KMS alias mapping for provisioning roles, (C) scale NAT and widen ephemeral ports to avoid retry storms. Who can push A?

nina_infra: pushing the firewall bypass now. Rule: `allow tcp 443 from sa-warm-pool-cidrs to keystore.internal:443 bypass-inspection=true comment="temp keystore bypass"
`

diag-bot: infra action: applied firewall passthrough in sa-east-1 (ruleset v2026.04.15.11) 10s to propagate.

sam_ops: applying temporary KMS alias mapping for assumed-role/spot-provisioner (4h TTL) to allow backlog to finish. Maria, can you log the change and ticket id?

maria_security: creating security ticket SC-900 and applying the temp alias mapping. Policy note (short): `allow kms:Decrypt for arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/spot-provisioner` (4h). Audit baseline recorded.

nina_infra: scaled NAT (added nat-0cafebabe) and set node sysctl port range to `10240 65535`. Propagation ~45s.

diag-bot: infra action: NAT created nat-0cafebabe, sysctl applied to autoscale group.

rachel_sre: warm pool trending up: 61% -> 93% in 9m. A few nodes show repeated reprovision attempts; marking them for manual reprovision.

sam_ops: good. Postmortem scope: (1) change sequencing checks: don't rotate KMS aliases at same time as inspection CA / policy changes, (2) add preflight keystore mutual-TLS handshake test that routes through any inspection appliance, (3) add alert when warm-pool <85% and ephemeral port usage >90%.

maria_security: follow-ups: (A) update change playbook to require eng-sre notification for any inspection rollouts, (B) formalize a short-lived alias fallback policy to avoid single-point prune failures, (C) request deeper audit hooks on the inspection appliance so it emits a record when it strips client certs. Filing SC-901 for those items.

diag-bot: uploaded pcaps and agent logs to s3://infra-dumps/sa-east-1/1767000000/ (pcap.tar.gz).

nina_infra: I'll draft the incident summary and schedule a 45-minute postmortem with security and infra. Keep the temp alias in place for 4h; Maria please remove after backlog cleared.

maria_security: temp alias will be removed at TTL expiry; I also recorded the explicit audit entries in SC-900. No suspicious KMS usage seen during window.
sam_ops: thanks everyone for quick response. We'll close after the postmortem doc and runbook updates. :thumbsup:
